The graph format changes (67); the first start after the upgrade rebuilds the graph.

## Changed behaviour

- **`watch` starts language servers only with `--lsp`.** A language server such as rust-analyzer runs the tree's build scripts and procedural macros, which a tree is not trusted to do unasked. Without `--lsp`, `watch` keeps the graph current from the native scanners.
- **The CLI refuses an unknown option or a value given to a flag** (`--dry-run=x`) and exits with status 2, instead of ignoring it.
- **A count argument to an MCP tool** that is negative, fractional, text or below its minimum (`max_nodes`, `max_lines` and every `limit` are at least 1) is answered with an error instead of the default.

## Resolution

- A call by bare name is linked only within its language family (C with C++, Objective-C and CUDA; JavaScript with TypeScript; Java with Kotlin, Scala and Groovy). A script calling `set` no longer reaches a Swift `set`, and C now reaches a C++ definition. Such placeholders are named `name from =family`.
- In Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Go a call without a receiver no longer links to a method, in its own file or another, and a Go call no longer leaves its package. A call through a value or through `self`/`this` still reaches the method.
- A call through `x()?.m()` is no longer read as a call of a free function `m`; a call of a closure or a parameter no longer links to a definition of the same name.
- A `~crate` scope reaches Rust definitions only; a SCIP index that misses a document no longer mints definitions for it, and a git-tracked or oversized `index.scip` is not read.
- Embeddings propagate through the whole graph, independent of the CPU count.

## Parsing

- A UTF-8 byte order mark no longer hides a file's first definition.
- C# verbatim strings, Lua long strings and level comments, Ruby `=begin` and C++ raw strings with an encoding prefix end where their language ends them.
- Long runs of `#` and deeply nested documentation comments are read in linear time, and long Elixir pipelines are bounded.

## Tools

- **`detect_changes`** and **`affected_tests`** read a diff with one git call per repository instead of three per file (a whole history against its root commit: 2.8 s to 0.7 s), and see files with non-ASCII names.
- **`cycles`** lists the tightest cycles first and says when the search was cut short (`truncated`); the search has a budget and no longer blocks the server on a large acyclic graph.
- Every field a tool returns is in its output schema; a request without a method and a batch get `-32600`; an unknown protocol version is answered with a supported one.
- **`change_history`** reports how many commits it actually read; **`affected_tests`** pages correctly past the end.
- Search weights a repeated query term once and lowercases Unicode; a document's repeated headings are numbered.

## Serving

- HTTP requests have a read deadline and bounded header lines; per-user tokens stay required once configured, even when the token file is emptied; the map checks the `Host` header and warns on a non-loopback bind.
- Under `watch`, compaction keeps which file each edge belongs to, so a later edit of that file replaces its edges instead of leaving stale ones.
- `/health`, `/ready` and `/metrics` of a server asleep after `--sleep-after` report the graph it will load again and its `indexed_at`, with `"asleep": true`.
- Files glasir writes into a tree (graph, audit log, map layout, hooks, client configs) are never written through a symbolic link; `install` keeps the key order of a client's JSON config and refuses a config whose server entry is not an object.
- git runs with fsmonitor, signature display, external diff and textconv switched off, and a repository whose local configuration sets a command-running key is refused.

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install attackwave/glasir/glasir`
- Scoop: add the bucket `Attackwave/scoop-glasir`, then run `scoop install glasir`
